title: Phelipeaux d'Herbault (Paris) to Philippe de Béthune (Rome), 13 February 1626, BnF fr. 3669 no. 25 (read from its twin no. 26)

steps.what: Fetched the Gallica IIIF manifest of fr. 3669 and the openings for pieces 24-27; fixed canvas = folio + 5 on ff. 70 and 73.
Catalogue task: check whether no. 26 is the decipherment of no. 25.

Clear text of nos. 25 and 26 compared: identical word for word; cipher runs fall after the same clear words; groups match at the two points checked (run 1 opening, run 3 ending). No group-for-group identity claimed.
Transcribed the letter with the interlinear decipherment of no. 26 for each cipher run (ct/letter_13feb1626.md); two proper names and 'Soubise' uncertain, a few glossed stretches left as '…'.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): decryption ct/letter_13feb1626.md (the twin no. 26's interlinear decipherment with the clear text); the cipher groups were never transcribed (project work).
Verification 5 (plain-bar rows): ct/letter_13feb1626.md had no ## Reading heading (header and cipher notes scored, plain 0.588); heading added, body plain 0.754, explicit 0.825. Keeps read.

outcome.method_basis: No. 25 (fr. 3669 ff. 69-71) is the same letter as no. 26 (ff. 72-74), which carries a contemporary interlinear decipherment three folios away; the reading is that decipherment.
outcome.notes: Read at the time: the reading is the contemporary decipherment on the twin copy, not an independent decryption. Unread in ct/letter_13feb1626.md: one whole run after 'les Anglois et les autres' ([chiffre: …]), ellipses inside the first and last passages; uncertain: Santriny, Montembelans, Soubise. Whether the letter or the series is in print was not checked.

credits.note: PR #3: found the decipherment on the twin copy no. 26, three folios away

texts.label: fr. 3669 no. 25 (deciphered from its twin no. 26), 13 Feb 1626
texts.summary: Raymond Phélypeaux d'Herbault, secretary of state, to Philippe de Béthune, ambassador at Rome, Paris 13 February 1626, on the eve of the Treaty of Monzón: the ciphered passages concern the Pope and the troops for the Valtelline, why the peace with the Huguenots was needed (the burden of a double war) and the withdrawal of the Dutch ships and the Huguenot fleet, and the prince of Piedmont's propositions pushing the King into war with Spain with Venice contributing.

reading_review.note: v5 check 23 Oct 2026 (1626 French: plain share is a bar too): the sweep scored the whole file, header and the cipher description included (plain 0.588, explicit 0.825). A '## Reading' heading now opens the letter text; body alone: plain 0.754 (43/57), explicit 0.825 (47/57). The failing sentences hold the decipherer's unread stretches and the expanded abbreviations mons[ieu]r etc. (each counted a part-word by the scorer), with names (Bevilacqua, Giraldi, Contarini). Rests on the contemporary interlinear decipherment of the twin copy no. 26. Keeps read.

texts.note: Decryption = the contemporary interlinear decipherment of the twin copy no. 26, transcribed with the clear text (ct/letter_13feb1626.md). No transcription of the cipher groups of no. 25 or no. 26 (project work).
